title: Micro-epoch trace cartography: sampling across traffic modes
content:
Purpose:
This is a working note describing a small exploratory pipeline we ran to map short-lived micro-epochs of traffic and their e2e latency signatures. Goal is to find stable stage fingerprints for microbursts and to test a lightweight classifier that flags ongoing micro-epoch types in the trace stream (coldstart vs warmed-kv vs tail-of-batch contention).

High-level summary: (short)
- Collected 72k traces sampled over 48 hours from 3 routes (chat-short, chat-long, embed-batch) with additional metadata (seq_len, model_variant, node_type).
- Computed per-trace stage timings by instrumenting the runtime at stage boundaries: tokenization, preproc, routing, batch-wait, model-forward, kv-lookup, kv-store, postproc, egress.
- Derived micro-epoch clusters using sliding-window aggregation (30s windows) and produced a cartography of 5 recurring micro-epoch types.
- Notable signals: micro-epoch type M3 shows p99 model-forward inflation tied to repeated KV-miss patterns; M5 shows batch-wait variance correlated with sudden QPS spike from a single tenant.

Methodology notes (collection):
- Trace sampler: 1:100 uniform sampling for baseline traffic + targeted up-sampling of high-seq_len (>1024) and coldstart traces (node boot events).
- Windowing: sliding 30s window with 10s step. Each window aggregated: qps, mean_seq_len, fraction_cold_starts, frac_kv_miss, mean_batch_size, p50/p95/p99 e2e latency.
- Stage timing extraction: hooks at stage enter/exit. For model-forward we capture subfields: forward-kernel, aten-mm, custom-attn (approx).
- Sanity: removed traces with missing stage markers (~2.8%) and traces with injected synthetic latency used in chaos testing windows.

Cohorts analyzed: (abbrev)
- chat-short: seq_len <= 64, typical payload small
- chat-long: seq_len 256-1024
- embed-batch: batch inference of embedding calls (1..8 per request)
- coldstart: first request to a freshly provisioned worker in last 45s

Aggregate quantiles (representative sample windows)
- chat-short (warm): p50=42ms, p95=118ms, p99=312ms
  stage breakdown (p99): tokenization 4ms, preproc 6ms, routing 8ms, batch-wait 22ms, model-forward 210ms, kv-lookup 24ms, postproc 5ms, egress 33ms
- chat-long (warm): p50=110ms, p95=260ms, p99=620ms
  stage breakdown (p99): tokenization 6ms, preproc 9ms, routing 12ms, batch-wait 28ms, model-forward 430ms, kv-lookup 52ms, postproc 9ms, egress 74ms
- embed-batch: p50=78ms, p95=320ms, p99=860ms
  stage breakdown (p99): tokenization 12ms, preproc 10ms, routing 16ms, batch-wait 140ms, model-forward 420ms, kv-lookup 22ms, postproc 10ms, egress 130ms
- coldstart (short-seq): p50=180ms, p95=540ms, p99=1600ms
  stage breakdown (p99): startup-init 430ms, tokenization 6ms, preproc 8ms, routing 14ms, batch-wait 18ms, model-forward 520ms, kv-lookup 32ms, postproc 10ms, egress 522ms

Interesting micro-epoch types (M1..M5):
- M1 (steady warm): low variance, predictable model-forward; dominant in baseline 70% of windows
- M2 (seqlen-swell): windows where mean_seq_len jumps >4x, model-forward scales ~linearly and kv-lookup stays low
- M3 (kv-churn): high fraction of KV-misses; model-forward p95/p99 show bimodal peaks (extra 150-300ms) due to synchronous fallback to remote-store and extra copy work
- M4 (contention-burst): batch-wait balloons; typical signature: batch-wait p99 >> model-forward p99; often caused by sudden single-tenant QPS spike (observed in two tenants)
- M5 (cold-start cluster): repeated short coldstarts due to preemptible node churn; heavy startup-init fraction, long tail in egress because clients retry

Representative anomaly case study: M3 window (2025-02-18T03:12:20 -> 03:12:50)
- QPS: 152 (baseline would be 47)
- Fraction_kv_miss: 0.62 (normal ~0.08)
- E2E p99 jump from 312ms -> 914ms on chat-short cohort
- Stage diffs: model-forward p99 increased by 320ms; kv-lookup p99 by 190ms. Traces show synchronous remote fetch in 64% of model-forward calls.
- Root cause hypothesis: cache eviction during a short rebalancing event; eviction TTL policy + concurrent compaction kicked in. Also observed compaction logs in node /var/log/kv/compactor at same timestamp.

Quick experiments run (results):
- Experiment A: increased local-cache size by 20% on a shadow pool (A/B across node-ips). Result: M3 frequency dropped 4x in the shadow pool, model-forward p99 dropped ~210ms on flagged windows.
- Experiment B: asynchronous remote fetch path enabled (background prefetch) on a canary. Result: e2e p99 improved for M3 but introduced extra memory pressure and occasional OOM on underprovisioned nodes (PR: #842).

Operational recommendations (short list):
1) Add a micro-epoch detector in the trace pipeline that tags windows with M3/M4/M5 signatures and escalates to a short-term mitigation: increased cache budget for affected nodes or temporarily route to warmed capacity.
2) Revisit compaction schedule to avoid overlapping heavy compactions with peak windows; add jittered compaction start times.
3) Make remote-fetch asynchronous with a bounded worker pool; implement backpressure to avoid OOMs.
4) Surface per-tenant QPS skew in the console and add per-tenant burst protection policy (burst token bucket with short-term smoothing).

Open questions / to validate:
- What exact sequence of cache eviction + compaction triggered the mass miss in M3? Need to correlate with KV metrics (eviction rates, compaction cycles).
- Are certain model variants more sensitive to synchronous remote fetch penalty (observed more in variant-v2-llama-8b-qdq)? Run a controlled AB with model pinned across variants.
- How does autoscaler react to these micro-epochs? Are nodes being unintentionally removed during bursts? (Check cluster-autoscaler logs).

Short list of queries / commands used (for reproducibility):
- trace-agg --from 2025-02-16T00:00 --to 2025-02-18T00:00 --sample 0.01 --window 30s --step 10s --stages tokenization,preproc,routing,batch-wait,model-forward,kv-lookup,postproc,egress > microepoch-window-agg.csv
- python analyses/cluster_windows.py --input microepoch-window-agg.csv --k 5 --out microepoch-clusters.json
- grep -n "compactor" /var/log/kv/* | sed -n '100,200p'  # correlated timestamps in node logs

Dashboard/visual artifacts planned:
- a 2D cartography plot (UMAP) colored by micro-epoch label with windows sized by p99-e2e
- timeline strip showing cluster label per 10s slice alongside cluster-autoscaler events and eviction metrics

Notes to self (informal):
- Need to add more labels to training data for automated detector (right now only 5k labeled windows).
- Ask infra for a snapshot of compaction config (cron schedule + last-run sizes) for the affected shard range.
- Miguel: follow up on PR #842 (async remote fetch) tradeoffs; can we add a guarded rollout + OOM detector?

Action items (owners):
- Priya: wire micro-epoch detector prototype into trace pipeline (ETA 2w)
- Jia: run AB test for variant sensitivity (ETA 1w)
- Miguel: review compaction jitter options with infra (ETA 1w)
- Ops: capture cluster-autoscaler logs around the two M4 incidents (requested)
